name: Input
description: A text input field with support for various input types and standard HTML input attributes
designIntent: The Input component provides a styled text input that follows the design system. It supports all standard HTML input attributes and includes proper focus states, disabled states, and file input styling.

props.name: type
props.description: HTML input type (text, password, email, number, etc.)

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text to display when input is empty

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input (controlled component)

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the input as required for form validation

props.name: onChange
props.description: Handler called when input value changes

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Handler called when input is focused

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Handler called when input loses focus

examples.title: Password input
examples.description: Input that obscures text for passwords

examples.title: Disabled input
examples.description: Input that cannot be interacted with

examples.title: File input
examples.description: Input for file uploads with styled file button

antiPatterns.title: Don't use Input for multi-line text
antiPatterns.description: Input is for single-line text. Use Textarea for multi-line content.

antiPatterns.title: Don't ignore validation
antiPatterns.description: Provide visual feedback for validation errors

antiPatterns.title: Don't use vague placeholders
antiPatterns.description: Placeholders should describe what input is expected

accessibility.implementation: Input is natively focusable and supports all keyboard input
Input type and placeholder are announced. Use aria-label or aria-labelledby for additional context
accessibility.userRequirements: For inputs without visible labels, use aria-label

accessibility.implementation: Supports HTML5 validation attributes (required, pattern, min, max)
accessibility.userRequirements: Use aria-invalid and aria-describedby for validation errors

accessibility.implementation: Disabled inputs are not focusable and screen readers announce as disabled
accessibility.userRequirements: Don't rely solely on visual disabled state

guidelines: Use descriptive placeholders that indicate expected input
Don't use placeholders as a replacement for labels
For required fields, consider adding '(required)' to placeholder or label
Always provide visible labels for inputs
Labels should be positioned above or before the input
For required fields, indicate this clearly
Labels should describe what the input is for, not what to type

compositionRules.relationship: Inputs should always have associated labels for accessibility
Inputs are typically used within form components for validation and submission
compositionRules.example: Form groups multiple inputs together for validation
